cells.tense: You can stand close to someone and learn what they need by tending it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Something you're still carrying for someone close finished a while back. Tell yourself, once, that it's over, and put it down. Keep only what's still growing, and give the week to that.
cells.core: You come to know someone close by watching what actually helps. You try something, it lands, you keep it. You don't decide who a person is in advance; the care itself tells you. People near you get looked after without having to ask, and that mostly works. Right now it's live and some of it has run its course. There's a weight you're still holding for someone that finished. Name it done, once, quietly, and set it down. Keep the one still growing and give the week to that one. Letting go won't look different from the outside. That's partly what it will teach you.
cells.sheetLine: You learn people by tending what actually helps them.
cells.verb: learning how things grow by tending them
cells.place: among people you are close to, where feeling-with happens

cells.tense: You will keep tending what you can't yet see, until the reaching outruns the person.
cells.act: explore the feeling with fresh sensitivity
cells.ask: Next time you catch yourself shaping how a closeness should go before it's happened, stop and feel what's actually here, with that person, however it is. Nothing to fix or plan. Then carry on.
cells.core: The picture of how it should go is running past the people themselves. You're already working on what you hope this becomes, the version that finally lands, and each try at securing it makes the next feel more necessary. It's wearing you thin, and from outside it reads as effort spent on something nobody asked for. There's another way in that doesn't require setting the care down. Feel toward what's actually here instead of what you're arranging: just who that person is right now, no plan attached. When the picture loses its grip, wonder comes back, and you can be with them rather than several steps beyond. It may not change what you do. It changes what you're doing it for.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping what hasn't happened yet, and it's wearing you thin.
cells.verb: learning how things grow by tending them
cells.place: among people you are close to, where feeling-with happens

cells.tense: The door to that closeness is behind you, and you are still standing at it.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Choose something that's only yours and begin it this week with no purpose attached. Not for anyone, not toward anything. Ten minutes, or as long as it holds you.
cells.core: The reach toward people close has gone quiet. You're still nearby, still kind, but the small offer, the question that finds out what someone needs, isn't happening much. You watch. You wait to be told. What you'd bring if you brought it has stopped being visible to you, and the distance stays where it is. Charging straight at the gap, feeling more toward people, empties a person further. Start something that lights you up for no useful reason — your own, nobody's business. Being visibly absorbed is what lets people find you again. Do it this week, once. Connection tends to follow someone already moving.
cells.sheetLine: You're kind and nearby, but you've stopped reaching first.
cells.verb: learning how things grow by tending them

cells.tense: The room is still being held together and you'd shrug and say you're just around.
cells.act: govern by knowing what to surrender
cells.ask: Think of a weight you carry for people close that's finished, and name it done to yourself. Then pick something you'll stop handling, and let it sit untouched.
cells.core: You set the pace, soften the bumps, and decide what gets said, and if someone asked you'd shrug and say you were only there. So your calls don't get counted as calls. You notice what each person needs and quietly act on it, in small ways, all the time. That's yours; it's been filed under having a good manner. Put a weight down where it can be seen. Take something you've been carrying for someone close that finished, and stop carrying it this week, not announced, just set down. Knowing what to let go of is the strongest thing you do with people. Once you've decided one thing is finished, that deciding is yours.
cells.sheetLine: You set the pace and call it just being around.
cells.verb: learning how things grow by tending them
cells.place: among people you are close to, where feeling-with happens
